title: Practice Questions Sheet 1
text:
ST201 · DATA ANALYSIS
  

  
    Practice Questions Sheet 1
  

    
    ST303 - Linear Models
  
  
    
    Lecturer: Cormac Monaghan
  
  
    
    This sheet provides practice with simple linear regression. You will work with the regression model algebraically, fit and interpret a model in R, and reproduce key regression calculations by hand. These practice questions should be attempted in your own time. These questions are not graded and should not be handed in
    You should attend the joint ST302/ST303 lab to get help with the questions and have your answers checked.
  
  





Simple linear regression
Consider the following simple linear regression model \[
y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1x_i + \epsilon_i, \qquad i = 1,\ldots,n.
\]
The above model may be alternatively written as
\[
y_i = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1(x_i-\bar{x}) + \epsilon_i, \qquad i = 1,\ldots,n.
\]
Answer the following:

Using the method of least squares, derive expressions for the estimators \(\hat{\alpha}_0\) and \(\hat{\alpha}_1\)
Interpret the parameters \(\alpha_0\) and \(\alpha_1\).
Explain why mean-centering the predictor variable can be useful.




Simple linear regression in R
As concrete cures, it gains strength overtime. The following data (see Table 1) represent the 7-day and 28-day strength, in pounds per square inch (psi), of a certain type of concrete.




Table 1: Concrete data





    

    

    
    
    
      
        
        
              
                7 Day
                28 Day
              
        
        
        
                
                  2300
                  4370
                
                
                  2430
                  4640

                  4620

                  4900

You can read the data from the RStudio server using:

# Using the `readr` and the `here` package.
# TIP: you can press tab when writing the folder path to have all the options
# folder / file options appear to you

concrete <- readr::read_csv(here::here("Sharedfiles/ST303/data/Concrete.csv"))

Answer the following set of questions using R

Create a scatterplot showing the relationship between 7-day strength on the \(x\)-axis and 28-day strength on the \(y\)-axis.
Does it seem appropriate to assume a linear relationship between the two variables (explain why you think so)?
Specify a simple linear regression model for these data algebraically.
Fit this model in R and report what the intercept, slope, and standard error for each term are.
In the context of this data, what do these values mean?
Update the scatter plot you made earlier to include a fitted line.




Simple linear regression by hand
This time, instead of using R, we will be calculating our linear regression parameters by hand. Using the concrete data we mentioned in Table 1, calculate the following:

\(\bar{x}\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\), and \(S_{xx}\).
\(\bar{y}\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n y_i^2\), and \(S_{yy}\).
\(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i\) and \(S_{xy}\).







TipYou may use R to verify your calculations.



However, in an exam setting you may be asked to do calculations by hand (hint, hint, wink, wink!!).
As such, please show all of your workings.


Use your calculated quantities to:

Calculate the least-squares slope estimate and the least-squares intercept estimate
In addition, calculate the estimated error variance.

title: Lecture overview
text:
Each class has a set of required readings that should be completed in your own time. For the most part, these readings will mirror what we have covered in the lectures. However, there will be times that I find a cool resource that I believe may be helpful for some of you.
All the slides for this module are special HTML files made using both Quarto and Clean Revealjs theme by Grant McDermott. Personally, this is my favourite theme to use for presentations, although I have made a couple of minor tweaks to it myself

title: Welcome to ST303
text:
Welcome to third year and welcome to ST303!
We will be covering lots of things related to linear models. This will range from the simple and multiple linear regression, ordinary and weighted least squares, inference, and diagnostics (among other things).


On successful completion of the module, you should be able to

Fit and interpret multiple regression models.
Understand the theory of multiple regression.
Assess model assumptions.
Use model diagnostics.




This module is broken down as 25% continuous assessment and 75% official exam.

4 assignments in the form of a Moodle quiz (worth 10%)
1 mid-term exam (worth 15%)
1 university exam (worth 75%)







NoteThe dates for each exam are still being finalised












ImportantDetails for Erasmus students



If you are an Erasmus student here for Semester 1 only (September - December), you will not be here for the final exam. With that in mind, your assignments and mid-term will be worth more marks.
If you are here for the full academic year (semester 1 AND semester 2), then your grades will follow the same breakdown as listed above.

Slides
All the slides for this module are created using Quarto. In fact, this entire module website is built using Quarto. Personally, I love Quarto. I do just about everything with it! If you every get a chance, do check it out (ok … mini rant over!)

There are many little hidden things you can do with these slides.
You can click in the slides and navigate through them with ← and →.
If you type ? (or shift + /) while viewing the slides you can see a list of slide-specific commands (such as like f for fullscreen mode or additionally s for presenter mode if you want to see my notes).
Finally, if you want to make a PDF of these slides you can press e, followed by ctrl + p.
